cards.explanation: The answer is the same devotion Paul has for them. Paul says, "But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you." (2 Corinthians 8:16) Paul doesn't take credit for it. He thanks God. Titus, Paul's partner and fellow worker, has the very same devotion Paul has.

The answer is True, friends! Paul says Titus "…is eagerly coming to you of his own volition." (2 Corinthians 8:17) Titus was glad to hear Paul's appeal, and he's coming eagerly on his own. Nobody had to drag him to the door.

The answer is gospel! Paul says this brother "…is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel." (2 Corinthians 8:18) The good news is what this man spends his work on. And every church praising him? That's a good name to have.

The answer is their eagerness to help. Paul says the offering is administered "…to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help." (2 Corinthians 8:19) It honors the Lord, and it shows how ready Paul's team is to help. Nothing in the verse says it's for anything else.

The answer is any criticism of how it's handled. Paul says, "We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift." (2 Corinthians 8:20) He wants the gift handled so well that nobody has a complaint about it. That's careful work, and I like it.

The answer is False, friends! Paul says, "For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men." (2 Corinthians 8:21) He cares about the Lord's eyes, and he cares about people's eyes too. Both count, and those two little words "not only" are the clue.

The answer is by his great confidence in the Corinthians. Paul says this brother has proven his earnestness "…many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you." (2 Corinthians 8:22) He has a long record already. Now he shows even more by believing in the Corinthians.
The answer is messengers, friends! Paul says, "As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ." (2 Corinthians 8:23) And what a title: the glory of Christ.

The answer is the proof of their love! Paul writes, "In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) That's what he asks the Corinthians to show, in full view of the churches. It's the second thing he names besides the reason for the boasting.

The answer is True, friends! Paul says, "Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you." (2 Corinthians 9:1) He says it because he knows their eagerness to help. The next verse spells that out.

The answer is that he knows how eager they are to help. Paul says, "For I know your eagerness to help…" (2 Corinthians 9:2) He already knows how ready they are, so there's no need to write about the gift. He trusts them.
The answer is stirred! Paul says, "And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise." (2 Corinthians 9:2) The Corinthians' eagerness got the Macedonians moving too. Zeal like that is catching.

The answer is so his boasting won't prove empty. Paul says, "But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said." (2 Corinthians 9:3) He's been boasting about the Corinthians. He wants them prepared so that boasting holds up.

The answer is False! Paul writes, "…we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident." (2 Corinthians 9:4) His team would feel it too, not just the Corinthians. They had put their confidence on the line.

The answer is generously and not begrudgingly, friends! Paul wants the brothers to "…make arrangements for the generous gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly." (2 Corinthians 9:5) The gift was already promised. He wants it prepared the right way, and generously is the word he uses.
